answer: Stop sybils with a timber shale comet: an agent stakes a bond for one timber stand. As a comet crosses, wardens time its pass over the shale ridge and mark the timber felled in that pass, voiding a stand whose pass is copied or claimed twice, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 passes at 21x: one comet crosses one shale line for one stand only, and its pass cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents fell once, keep rights.
